reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

SFLOW-V5-x-1.note: single-polarity: the header's first field decodes big-endian to 5, the only datagram_version the XDR union defines; WriteDatagramHeader writes a constant, so any other value fails the assertion

SFLOW-V5-x-10.note: Single-polarity row. TestSFlowV5SamplingRateIsTheSourceRate drives the real EncodeFlowSample with two sources at 74565 and 1000 and requires each datagram's sampling_rate to equal its source's rate, so a constant, a stale rate or a literal goes red (recorded). sampling_worker.go fills FlowSample.Rate from the psample packet's rate.

SFLOW-V5-x-11.note: asserts the code's estimate sample_pool = min(seq*rate, MaxUint32), not the RFC's 'Total number of packets that could have been sampled'; no packet count the data source saw is observed, and the saturation subtest asserts behaviour the RFC does not state (an XDR unsigned counter wraps; a saturated pool stops advancing)

SFLOW-V5-x-12.note: positive: ifIndex 0x01000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF decode unchanged from expanded counter format 4 and flow format 3; negative: indexes at and above 2^24 never alias to their low 24 bits in source_id_index or if_counters.ifIndex

SFLOW-V5-x-14.note: positive: a snapshot one full interval after the last poll produces a counter sample; but the negative asserts that a snapshot before the interval is suppressed, and the RFC makes the interval a maximum and lets the agent sample early, so the negative does not violate this requirement; no unit shows a poll is produced when the maximum interval elapses without an admitting snapshot

SFLOW-V5-x-15.note: single-polarity (marker: interfaceCountersFrom has no differencing path): a second conversion of the same kernel stats must equal the first, so a delta implementation (which loses the traffic of a lost sample) fails 'second conversion differs'; the negligible-wrap clause rests on 64-bit octet counters, and RxBytes 5e9 > 2^32 must come through untruncated

SFLOW-V5-x-16.note: Integer clause now proven: TestSFlowV5UnknownEgressInterfaceIsZero requires output format 0 and value 0 for a sample with no egress (recorded); sampling_worker.go never sets FlowSample.Output, so every egress is unknown and sent as 0. Counter clause: TestSFlowV5UnavailableCountersCarrySentinelEveryPoll and TestSFlowV5AvailableCountersNeverTurnUnavailable assert 0xFFFFFFFF for the four unexposed counters and real values otherwise, but neither carries a discrimination record, so that clause's red is unobserved.

SFLOW-V5-x-2.note: the quote carries four clauses (loopback on a multi-homed agent, SNMP connectivity, invariance across interface reconfiguration, a unique long-lived key); TestSFlowDatagramHeaderIPv4 only asserts that the address handed to WriteDatagramHeader reaches bytes 8-11 in one call, so an exporter that picked a non-loopback or per-interface address, or changed it when an interface went down, passes; no assertion goes red on any of the four

SFLOW-V5-x-25.note: positive: one sample yields exactly one datagram sent at once; negative: three samples yield three datagrams, the sender count advancing by one each, and no datagram carries more than one flow_sample

SFLOW-V5-x-26.note: both units call writeCounterDatagrams directly and prove that a 30-source batch is packed into three returned datagrams with none left over; neither observes a datagram being SENT, and the condition of the quote (counters due because the maximum sampling interval elapsed) is never produced, so an exporter that never sent a poll when the interval ran out passes; the trigger is SFLOW-V5-x-14, itself weak

SFLOW-V5-x-27.note: Ze cannot promise its ifIndex stays below 2^24 (Linux ifindex is a full int), so it falls in the quote's 'Otherwise' branch and the compact-for-all clause does not bind it; mixing: a compact format 1 or 2 among the six records fails 'compact data_format emitted'; expanded for all: alternating low and full-width ifIndex values fail 'want expanded 4' and 'want expanded 3' if any interface drops to compact

SFLOW-V5-x-28.note: Per-source clause: TestSFlowV5FlowSequencePerSourceID interleaves sources 3 and 4 and requires 1,2,3 and 1,2, so one sequence shared across source_ids goes red (recorded). Reset clause: TestSFlowV5PoolAndSequenceResetTogether and TestSFlowV5PoolNeverResetsWithoutSequence (both recorded).

SFLOW-V5-x-29.note: Reset clause now whole: TestSFlowV5SequenceResetOnAnyCounterGoingBack rewinds each of the 13 cumulative if_counters in turn and requires sequence 1, with 2 on the prior rising poll (recorded, countersWentBackwards). The per-source_id increment clause (a second source's reset leaves the first untouched) and the no-reset-without-discontinuity negative rest on TestSFlowV5SequenceNeverResetWithoutDiscontinuity and TestSFlowV5SequenceResetWithCounters, which carry no discrimination record.

SFLOW-V5-x-3.note: single-polarity: agent_address and sub_agent_id 7 both decode to the distinct values written, so the pair the header carries names the sub-agent's datagram stream

SFLOW-V5-x-30.note: positive: a CounterGeneration change with rising counters resets the sequence to 1; negative: an unchanged generation keeps 1,2,3 even when a counter reads lower

SFLOW-V5-x-31.note: TestSFlowV5DataSourceKeepsOneSubAgent shows one collector's factories send source 3's counter and flow samples under its single sub-agent 7, twice (recorded). Not proven, and likely a defect: sub-agent-id is per collector (config.go CollectorConfig.SubAgentID, no cross-collector validation), so two sflow collectors with the same agent-address and different sub-agent-id export one data source under two sub-agents of one agent. TestSFlowV5SubAgentBindingConstantForSession still sends source 3 under 7 then 8 and calls it a new session. Needs the owner's design choice (agent-level sub-agent-id, or a config validator).

SFLOW-V5-x-32.note: positive: every counter unavailable on the first poll is still the sentinel on a poll with different statistics; negative: available counters stay available on a later zero-valued poll

SFLOW-V5-x-33.note: positive: the flow_sample carries one sampled_header record with the 14 captured bytes; negative: a 1500-byte capture that cannot fit is truncated but still carried as a non-empty sampled_header prefix

SFLOW-V5-x-34.note: positive: a 60-octet skb gives frame_length 64 and stripped 4, the FCS added to both; negative: over 64, 1500 and 9000 octets frame_length minus stripped is always the skb length

SFLOW-V5-x-4.note: single-polarity (marker: the exporter holds no path that emits a datagram without advancing): writeCounterDatagrams' two datagrams carry sequence 1 and 2 and return 3 as the next, so a sender that did not increment per datagram fails seq2 != 2 and nextSeq != 3

SFLOW-V5-x-5.note: positive proves a counter batch splits at the 1400-byte default buffer (11+4 samples), but the bound is len(buf) and only the default is exercised: an encoder that ignored the collector's configured max-datagram-size and hard-coded 1400 would pass, and Sender.Send's refusal of an oversized payload is not in this unit; the size assertion itself cannot fail because dg is a slice of buf

SFLOW-V5-x-6.note: the unit hands the sample to a stub encoder and asserts only that the exporter dispatched it synchronously; it never observes the real FlowEncoder or Sender putting the datagram on the wire within 1 second, so a buffering encoder would pass (x-25's units observe the real send)

SFLOW-V5-x-7.note: Improved but not whole. TestSFlowV5FlowDatagramIsXDR pins the datagram header words, the flow_sample length, header_length, and the zero padding after 13 sampled-header octets (recorded); TestSFlowIfCounters pins the if_counters record (no record). Still unasserted under x-7: the counters_sample wrapper words written by writeCounterSample (tag, length, sequence, source_id, record count), the other flow_sample words (sample_pool, drops, input, output are checked for value elsewhere but not tagged x-7), and the extended_gateway record's variable-length arrays and next-hop union (writeExtendedGateway).

SFLOW-V5-x-9.note: positive: counter and flow datagrams of one sender share one datagram sequence that wraps through 0xFFFFFFFF; negative: a counter generation reset restarts only the source sample sequence, never the datagram sequence
